description: Rank NYC's residential neighborhoods by what a family cares about — the same ranking as Best fit on motley.nyc. Pass ranked priority words, most important first: families, schools, affordability, character, getting-around, safety, air-and-health (and synonyms such as crime, rent, transit, commute, kids), plus two factors — parks or playgrounds (the share of homes within a 10-minute walk of an NYC Parks playground) and diversity (how evenly residents spread across five census groups). Or pass per-metric weights for the seven scores. Optionally scope to one borough. Returns the top neighborhoods with a fit score and the score breakdown, which factors counted, any priority words we don't measure (relay them — they added nothing), and a best_fit_url that opens the same ranking on motley.nyc. A deterministic weighted sort over neighborhood-level data, not a per-child school match.

borough.description: Restrict the ranking to one borough

limit.description: How many top neighborhoods to return

min_population.description: Residential floor — drops parks/cemeteries/airports that score ~100 by having almost no residents (default 1000).

priorities.description: What the family cares about, most important first — e.g. ["parks","schools","safety"]. Score words: families, schools, affordability, character, getting-around, safety, air-and-health (and synonyms like crime, rent, transit, commute, kids). Factor words: parks or playgrounds (homes near an NYC Parks playground), diversity. Weighted 1, ½, ⅓… by position. Words we don't map come back in `unrecognized_priorities`.

weights.description: Per-metric importance (0+; higher = matters more). Any subset; normalized internally. When given, it sets the seven scores and the score words in `priorities` are ignored; the factor words (parks, diversity) in `priorities` still count.

name: rank-neighborhoods
